name: Patricia Brown
chief_complaint: Sharp right-sided chest pain and shortness of breath for 2 days
opening_statement: I've had this sharp pain in my right chest for the past two days, and I'm finding it harder to breathe, especially when I take a deep breath. I'm really worried something serious is wrong.
emotional_baseline: Anxious and worried, seeking reassurance but cooperative

symptoms.character: Sharp, stabbing pain worse on deep inspiration
symptoms.radiation: No radiation, localized to right lower chest
symptoms.associations: Worse with coughing, deep breathing, and movement
symptoms.exacerbating_factors: Deep breathing, coughing, lying on right side

symptoms.character: Shortness of breath, worse on exertion
symptoms.associations: Associated with chest pain, no wheeze
symptoms.severity: Breathless after 10 steps, previously could walk 2km daily

respiratory.auscultation: Reduced air entry right base, occasional fine creps right lower zone, no wheeze

cardiovascular.auscultation: Dual heart sounds, no murmurs, no added sounds

lower_limbs.palpation: Mild tenderness right calf, no palpable cord, negative Homan's sign
lower_limbs.peripheral_pulses: All pulses palpable and equal bilaterally

examination_findings.abdominal: Soft, non-tender, no organomegaly, bowel sounds present
examination_findings.neurological: Alert and oriented, no focal deficits

bedside.result: Sinus tachycardia 102 bpm, S1Q3T3 pattern present, no ST changes
bedside.significance: S1Q3T3 suggestive but not diagnostic of PE

bedside.result: pH 7.44, PaO2 72 mmHg, PaCO2 32 mmHg, HCO3 22 mmol/L, A-a gradient 38 mmHg
bedside.significance: Type 1 respiratory failure, increased A-a gradient consistent with V/Q mismatch

pathology.significance: Elevated, warrants imaging in moderate-high pretest probability
Normal, no evidence of myocardial injury

imaging.result: Subsegmental filling defect in right lower lobe posterior basal segmental artery (A10). No larger proximal thrombus. No evidence of right heart strain.
imaging.significance: Confirms subsegmental PE. Low thrombus burden, clinical significance debated.

imaging.result: Non-occlusive thrombus right posterior tibial vein, calf veins patent
imaging.significance: Source of embolism identified, distal DVT

scoring.result: 6.5 points (Clinical signs of DVT 3, PE most likely diagnosis 3, Tachycardia 1.5, Recent immobilization <3 days -1.5)
Does not apply (age >50 criterion not met, but tachycardia present)
scoring.interpretation: PERC not applicable, proceed to D-dimer/imaging

expected_management.rationale: Direct oral anticoagulant preferred for uncomplicated PE in stable patient
expected_management.pbs_restriction: PBS authority required - subsegmental PE may require justification, document symptomatic + distal DVT

expected_management.rationale: Ensure adherence, monitor for bleeding complications

critical_errors.detection: If candidate suggests observation only or delayed anticoagulation pending specialist review

critical_errors.consequence: Ongoing prothrombotic stimulus, recurrent VTE risk >50%, auto-fail
critical_errors.detection: If candidate does not explicitly stop COC in management plan

fracp_reviews.credentials: FRACP (Respiratory), Staff Specialist, Royal Melbourne Hospital
fracp_reviews.comments: Excellent medium-difficulty case. Subsegmental PE management remains controversial but this scenario appropriately balances evidence (symptomatic patient + distal DVT warrants treatment per 2023 eTG). The COC cessation is the critical error most candidates miss. Wells score calculation is accurate. Consider adding mention of PESI score for risk stratification, though not essential for this stable patient. DOAC choice (apixaban) is appropriate - avoid rivaroxaban in this age group due to higher bleeding risk in young women. Overall, clinically authentic and tests key decision-making.

fracp_reviews.credentials: FRACP (General Medicine & Haematology), VMO, Austin Health
fracp_reviews.comments: Well-constructed persona with appropriate comorbidity burden for medium difficulty. The Factor V Leiden context is realistic (heterozygous, provoked VTE) and reflects common clinical scenarios. Anticoagulation duration is appropriately deferred to haematology - heterozygous FVL + provoked event typically warrants 3-6 months, not lifelong. The recent long-haul flight is a clear precipitant. Good inclusion of subtle exam findings (S1Q3T3, mild calf asymmetry). One teaching point: subsegmental PE controversy centres on isolated subsegmental PE without DVT - this case has concurrent distal DVT which strengthens treatment indication. Critical errors are correctly weighted.
fracp_reviews.suggested_changes: Optional: Add PESI score (likely Class I-II). Otherwise approved as-is.

learning_objectives.objective: Apply Wells Score for PE and interpret pretest probability in clinical decision-making
learning_objectives.clinical_relevance: High-yield for AMC Clinical Exam - Wells score informs imaging pathway (score >4 → CTPA, score <4 → D-dimer first)

learning_objectives.objective: Recognize absolute contraindication to combined oral contraceptives in thrombophilia + VTE
learning_objectives.clinical_relevance: Critical safety issue - COC increases VTE risk 3-6 fold, absolute contraindication with known thrombophilia or VTE history

learning_objectives.objective: Differentiate management of subsegmental PE with vs without concurrent DVT
learning_objectives.clinical_relevance: Controversial area - isolated subsegmental PE may be observed in select cases, but presence of DVT mandates anticoagulation per eTG 2023

learning_objectives.objective: Select appropriate DOAC and dosing regimen for acute PE
learning_objectives.clinical_relevance: Apixaban preferred in young women (lower bleeding risk than rivaroxaban). Standard regimen: 10mg BD x 7d then 5mg BD. Duration determined by haematology.

learning_objectives.objective: Identify risk factors for VTE: Factor V Leiden, COC use, recent long-haul travel
learning_objectives.clinical_relevance: Essential for AMC exam - candidates must recognize multiplicative risk (heterozygous FVL + COC increases VTE risk 8-16 fold, travel adds transient risk)

learning_objectives.objective: Interpret CTPA findings and correlate with clinical presentation
learning_objectives.clinical_relevance: Subsegmental PE definition: thrombus in 4th-5th order pulmonary arteries (segmental or smaller). Absence of RV strain (RV/LV ratio <1) indicates low-risk PE.

learning_objectives.objective: Formulate evidence-based discharge plan including anticoagulation monitoring and specialist referral
learning_objectives.clinical_relevance: Comprehensive management includes: (1) DOAC initiation, (2) COC cessation, (3) haematology referral for duration, (4) GP follow-up, (5) patient education on bleeding risks

learning_objectives.objective: Apply MBS billing codes for PE investigation and management
learning_objectives.clinical_relevance: Australian context essential - MBS 57360 (CTPA), MBS 132 (specialist review), PBS authority for apixaban in subsegmental PE (may require clinical justification)
